questions.q: What is the overall goal of this capstone project?
options: To predict the future direction of ZQX Inc.'s stock price
To price a small options portfolio with Black-Scholes, compute its Greeks, aggregate them, and size a hedge trade that flattens portfolio delta
To design a brand-new options exchange
To calculate the historical VaR of the S&P 500
questions.explain: The capstone's concrete deliverables are: Black-Scholes prices for each option, each option's Greeks, portfolio-level aggregated Greeks, and a hedge trade sized to bring portfolio delta to zero.

questions.q: What does it mean that Option C in the portfolio is a 'short' position?
options: Option C has a shorter time to expiry than the other two options
The portfolio has written (sold) those puts rather than bought them
Option C has a lower strike price than the others
Option C cannot be priced using Black-Scholes
questions.explain: A short position means the puts were sold (written) rather than purchased, which is why Option C's contribution to portfolio Greeks carries a flipped sign compared to the long call positions.

questions.q: What does the standard '100-share' contract multiplier mean for this portfolio?
options: Each option contract covers 100 shares of the underlying
Only 100 shares of ZQX Inc. exist in total
The portfolio must hold at least 100 different options
Each option expires in 100 days
questions.explain: By standard convention, one option contract covers 100 shares of the underlying stock, which is why position-level Greeks scale each per-share Greek by 100 times the number of contracts.

questions.q: Why is delta chosen as the specific hedge target for this capstone, rather than gamma or vega?
options: Because delta is usually the largest single directional risk in an options book, and a share of stock has a delta of exactly 1, making it directly offsettable
Because gamma and vega cannot be calculated for any option
Because delta is the only Greek regulators require firms to hedge
Because flattening delta automatically flattens gamma and vega as well
questions.explain: Delta represents directional exposure and is typically the largest single risk. Since a share has delta exactly 1, shares can directly offset a portfolio's net delta — though gamma and vega exposure remain afterward.

questions.q: After the hedge trade in Lesson 32 flattens the portfolio's delta, what will still remain, according to this lesson's setup?
options: Nothing — the portfolio becomes completely risk-free
Only credit risk from the options counterparty
Gamma and vega exposure, since delta-hedging does not eliminate those
The portfolio's strike prices will all change automatically
questions.explain: Flattening delta removes first-order directional exposure but does not eliminate gamma (how delta itself changes) or vega (sensitivity to volatility), which Lesson 33 addresses directly.
